chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub and Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darrāj and Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
There is no wudu (ablution) in kissing, nor in direct bodily contact, nor in touching the private part.

key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: ritual ablution required for acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Do kissing, bodily contact, or touching the private part invalidate wudu in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that kissing, direct bodily contact, and touching the private part do not necessitate wudu (ablution). It relates to rulings of ritual purity and clarifies acts that do not invalidate wudu.
